title: Rigveda 6.73: To Brihaspati
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 6.73: To Brihaspati: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 6.73 is a hymn of 3 verses addressed to Brihaspati. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 6, the family book of Bharadvāja. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 489v. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 6.73.1-3 (aṣṭaka 5, adhyāya 1, varga 17); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 489v
translation.original_text:
1yo a̍dri̱bhit pra̍thama̱jā ṛ̱tāvā̱ bṛha̱spati̍r āṅgira̱so ha̱viṣmā̍n | dvi̱barha̍jmā prāgharma̱sat pi̱tā na̱ ā roda̍sī vṛṣa̱bho ro̍ravīti ||
2janā̍ya ci̱d ya īva̍ta u lo̱kam bṛha̱spati̍r de̱vahū̍tau ca̱kāra̍ | ghnan vṛ̱trāṇi̱ vi puro̍ dardarīti̱ jaya̱ñ chatrū̍m̐r a̱mitrā̍n pṛ̱tsu sāha̍n ||
3bṛha̱spati̱ḥ sam a̍jaya̱d vasū̍ni ma̱ho vra̱jān goma̍to de̱va e̱ṣaḥ | a̱paḥ siṣā̍sa̱n sva1̱̍r apra̍tīto̱ bṛha̱spati̱r hanty a̱mitra̍m a̱rkaiḥ ||
translation.text:
1SERVED with oblations, first-born, mountain-render, Angiras' son, Br̥ihaspati, the Holy, With twice-firm path, dwelling in light, our Father, roars loudly, as a bull, to Earth and Heaven.
2Br̥ihaspati, who made for such a people wide room and verge when Gods were invocated, Slaying his enemies, breaks down their castles, quelling his foes and conquering those who hate him.
3Br̥ihaspati in war hath won rich treasures, hath won, this God, the great stalls filled with cattle. Striving to win waters and light, resistless, Br̥ihaspati with lightning smites the foeman.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 489v (numbered 10v by the scribe) (OPenn image 490, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 6.72.4 ‹pakvam āmāsu antaḥ ni›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 490r (numbered 11r by the scribe), begins in RV 6.74.1 ‹sapta ratnā dadhānā śam›. Verses 6.73.1-3 end on this page.

1yaḥ | adri-bhit | prathama-jāḥ | ṛta-vā | bṛhaspatiḥ | āṅgirasaḥ | haviṣmān | dvibarha-jmā | prāgharma-sat | pitā | naḥ | ā | rodasī iti | vṛṣabhaḥ | roravīti
2janāya | cit | yaḥ | īvate | oṃ iti | lokam | bṛhaspatiḥ | deva-hūtau | cakāra | ghnan | vṛtrāṇi | vi | puraḥ | dardarīti | jayan | śatrūn | amitrān | pṛt-su | sāhan
3bṛhaspatiḥ | sam | ajayat | vasūni | mahaḥ | vrajān | go--mataḥ | devaḥ | eṣaḥ | apaḥ | sisāsan | svaḥ | aprati-itaḥ | bṛhaspatiḥ | hanti | amitram | akairḥ
